summary: Build and host an online AI chatbot called "Shriram Chess Assistant" to answer chess rules questions across formats, provide learning examples with board/move visualization, operate as a text-first (just words) app, and be easily shareable with friends via WhatsApp.
architectural_notes: Product: text-first chat app with optional chessboard/move visualization for learning examples.
Distribution: provide a shareable public URL and WhatsApp sharing entry point.
known_issues: Build/app generation failed when attempting to add the WhatsApp share button; user requested retry.
Basic checkmate learning example contains incorrect/illegal bishop and queen moves; user requested full review and correction of all example moves.

existing_features.title: Create a text-first chat experience titled "Shriram Chess Assistant" that lets users ask questions about chess rules (all formats) and receive answers in English.

Implement a deterministic (non-LLM) chess rules assistant engine that answers common chess-rules questions across formats (e.g., standard/classical, rapid, blitz, bullet) and includes coverage for: legal moves, check/checkmate, stalemate, castling, en passant, promotion, draw rules (threefold repetition, 50/75-move, insufficient material, agreement), touch-move guidance as a general concept, time controls, and basic tournament/online variations. Responses must be safe, factual, and include brief examples when helpful.

Add a “Chess Learning Assistant” mode that can present examples with a visible chessboard and step-by-step moves. The user must be able to trigger an example from chat (e.g., via a button/suggested prompt like “Show an example”) and then see a board with a move list that can be stepped through (Next/Previous) with highlighted last move.

Provide a clear “Host online” help section inside the app explaining how the app is hosted as an Internet Computer canister and how the user can obtain/share the public URL after deployment (in English).
Add a WhatsApp sharing flow that lets the user share the app link with friends by opening WhatsApp with a prefilled message containing the deployed app URL.

Apply a cohesive, creative visual theme appropriate for a chess learning assistant (avoid blue/purple by default), including typography, spacing, and a consistent component style across chat, learning mode, and hosting/share sections.

Fix the build/generation failure related to the WhatsApp sharing UI so the app builds successfully and the existing Share menu in the header reliably supports both “Share on WhatsApp” (opens WhatsApp with a prefilled message containing the current deployed app URL) and “Copy Link” (copies the current URL and shows a success/error toast). All user-facing text must be in English.
Publish the current Shriram Chess Assistant build by running a clean build and deployment so the app is accessible via its public canister URL, and verify that in-app sharing uses the deployed URL.
Replace the app logo shown in the header with a new logo asset for Shriram Chess Assistant.
Add the new logo image file(s) as static frontend assets under frontend/public/assets/generated and ensure they are referenced directly (not served via the backend).

Fully review and correct all Chess Learning Assistant examples in frontend/src/features/learning/examples.ts so that every step-to-step transition represents a legal chess move for the piece being moved, and each step’s board position, move text, and lastMove coordinates are consistent with each other (including the “Scholar's Mate (Basic Checkmate)” example where bishop/queen moves were reported incorrect).

Add a lightweight runtime validation for learning examples that runs in development (and/or at app startup) to detect invalid example data (e.g., lastMove not matching the board diff, illegal piece movement, or inconsistent move notation vs. coordinates), and present a clear English error message in the Learning UI if an example is invalid so incorrect examples are not silently shown.

new_feature_requests.summary: Create AI chatbot named "Shriram Chess Assistant" to answer queries about chess rules across all formats.
Provide guidance/setup to host the chatbot online for public access.
Add chess learning mode with examples showing a chessboard and moves.
Build as a text-first "just words" app (simple chat UI).
Enable easy sharing with friends via WhatsApp (share link / WhatsApp share flow).
Change/update the app logo (branding update for Shriram Chess Assistant).

Fully review and correct all Chess Learning Assistant example moves (including basic checkmate) to ensure bishop/queen and all piece moves follow chess rules; update the app with corrected examples and rebuild.
